slot_note: fourth root of task130 (wave 1, re-root: retired): v1 and v2 failed on the portal, v3 was landed in house because its default construction was the golden; same objective, new subdomain, new graded quantity, new Layer 2 pitfall
niche: first-year funding of a health system's new self-insured professional liability trust that each hospital and the employed medical group joins, claims-made, on the day its commercial occurrence policy expires
stakeholder_role: vice president of risk management and insurance at a regional health system, who recommends the trust's first-year contribution to the board

spine.entity: one employed or contracted clinician's paid full-time equivalent in one month, with the entity, cost centre and specialty payroll held for that month

world.org_type: nonprofit regional health system with four hospitals and an employed medical group, replacing commercial occurrence professional liability policies with a self-insured claims-made trust

driver: A cover that pays only for events that both occur and are first reported inside its own window is costed from a full period's cost per unit of exposure, when inside a short window only the events reported soon after they occur can count and here those are the cheap ones; the expected cost is the exposure at each point of the window times the cost of past events reported within the time then left, which neither a full period's cost, its prorated share nor the share of events reported within a year at the average cost gives.
driver_concrete: Each hospital and the employed medical group joins the new trust, claims-made, on the day its commercial occurrence policy expires, so the trust's 2027 cost is the claims first made by 31 December 2027 from incidents after each entity's transition; the system's early-resolution programme turns most claims into quick, small settlements while the lawsuits that carry most of the money are made years after the incident, so the expected cost is each month's covered clinician exposure times the trended cost of the system's past claims made within the months then left in 2027, not a mature year's cost per FTE prorated to each entity's months.
stump: A competent solver collapses the claims system's defendant rows to one claim per incident, values and trends every claim, takes the system's annual claims cost per clinician FTE by specialty, prorates it to each entity's months in the trust and funds several times the golden; the step that lands it there is costing the trust's opening months as a mature year, when only claims made before 31 December 2027 from incidents after each transition count, and those are the system's quick, cheap early-resolution claims.
analyst_test: a strong analyst who dedupes the claims and reads the trust agreement and funding policy correctly still multiplies a mature year's cost per FTE by each entity's 2027 months of cover, or applies the share of claims made within a year of the incident at the average claim cost, and overfunds the trust, because inside a first claims-made window only the claims made quickly count and they cost a fraction of the average.
domain_test: the deciding quantity is the expected cost of claims first made inside a claims-made trust's opening window, built from each entity's covered clinician exposure through the system's own report-lag and cost-by-lag experience, which is how a professional liability actuary funds a first claims-made year; with another field's nouns the retroactive dates, report lags, early-resolution settlements and specialty classes have nothing to attach to.

differentiation.task102: task102 moves payments across a period boundary by a business-day release rule; here nothing moves across a boundary: a claims-made window keeps only the claims made soon after their incident, which are the cheap early-resolution ones, so the cost is the exposure at each point of each entity's months of cover times the cost of past claims made within the time then left.
differentiation.task501: task501 v3 sized a buffer on the furthest a cumulative path ran ahead of its forecast inside a test horizon; here no path maximum or buffer is involved: the cost of a claims-made opening window is a lag-truncated, cost-weighted share of exposure, entity by entity.

lineage.fate: failed on the portal 2026-10-10: both top models filed the golden seven-section designation
lineage.driver: The committed set is read off holdings on a future effective date built forward from a past snapshot of filed returns; the forward roll, with a third party's takeovers of scheduled transfers completed on the fixed interval its settled cases show, reproduces both closed controls because every holder enrolled by the snapshot had filed, but the holder population on the effective date also takes in holders enrolled after the snapshot who have not filed yet, whose units are recoverable only by grouping the transfer extract on the buyer, so a unit the roll leaves under the threshold is over it.

lineage.fate: failed on the portal 2026-10-11 (the model built the filed duty-date queue and filed the golden 46 units); hardening loop 1 (lists on the need re-derived from the household members on each round day against a lagging case record) rejected at the clone pre-flight as a Template of task73 world ten, and the same move was solved on the portal in task86 v2's first cut
lineage.driver: Members of a closed group leave only when a rationed supply reaches them, and the supply is handed out across a wider list in a filed priority order within each size class, so how many remain at a later date is each member's rank inside its class against the cumulative planned supply, and neither a leaving rate nor a survival curve read off history, which both average over whatever list length the past happened to have, gives it.

lineage.fate: rejected at the clone pre-flight (Template, Track B, against task73 world ten)
lineage.driver: A waiting list is split into classes by an attribute the governing rule works out on the day from each member's composition, while the case record keeps that attribute as last assessed; a run-off forecast against a planned supply has to recompute every member's class on each allocation day, because members age across the rule's thresholds and a record assessed years earlier holds the longest-waiting members in classes they have already left.

lineage.fate: landed by the in-house solver in round 1 on 2026-10-11 (the analog cohort's tier PMPM, trended and count-weighted, in about four minutes); hardening loop 1 found no forced, fork-free deeper rung; the number was retired with three architectures spent and put back in the author's wave 1 as a fourth root
lineage.driver: A group chosen for an extreme value of a noisy outcome in one period is forecast for the next period by carrying its own chosen-period value forward with trend, when the outcome regresses toward the mean; the forecast that holds is the next-period experience of a group chosen the same way one period earlier, which the record contains untreated, cell by cell.

Pattern none, decisive G13 (horizon: the window the decision covers) then G14 (cost conditioned on early reporting). Calibration none: the system's own claims experience is the evidence, no organ. context_artifact operations_log: the risk management claims system export the stakeholder works from.
layer1: a risk management claims system export with one row per named defendant, so one incident naming a surgeon, an anaesthetist and the hospital is three rows under one claim number
two expiring commercial carriers' loss runs in their own layouts (one per policy period, a format change when a carrier moved systems in 2021) overlapping the claims system
claim stages that move (an early-resolution request that later becomes a suit keeps its first claim-made date), reopened claims and claims closed without indemnity but with defence costs
paid indemnity and defence costs on a transaction ledger, with case reserves on open claims at the valuation date
payroll FTE by clinician and month with specialty and cost-centre codes that were re-mapped in 2020, employed and contracted clinicians in one file, and clinicians moving between entities
the early-resolution programme's own case log keyed on its case number, linked to claim numbers only once a payment or demand exists
each entity's expiring policy period, transition date and the trust's coverage terms in separate documents
